doc.title: Dan Morgenstern interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 9, 2013

title: Turning down liner notes he did not care for
summary: He could refuse assignments of music he had no feeling for.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Did you ever have to write — did you ever take on an assignment to write liner notes for music that you really didn’t care for?

Not really. I did have – I mean since I was not — except for that brief period when I was with Jazz magazine — maybe you could say that I depended on it as a main source of income for me, but I could afford to say no. I mean no, I didn’t want to write about anything that I didn’t care for. Why? I mean you would try to sell somebody a bill of goods. Honestly, there may be music that was very good in and of itself but I just had no particular connection with it and no particular feeling for it, I would turn it down.
